Eight stages, and you always know which one you are in.

We tell you which stage is likely to be the long one on your project before you sign anything.

  1. 01

    Consultation

    Week 1

    We walk the property, talk through what you actually want to change, and give you an honest read on scope and budget before anyone quotes a number.

  2. 02

    Site evaluation

    Weeks 1–2

    Flood zone, High-Velocity Hurricane Zone requirements, permit history, HOA or historic review, and what is behind the walls.

  3. 03

    Design and planning

    Weeks 2–5

    Layouts, finishes and system choices, with the real trade-offs explained rather than one pre-set package.

  4. 04

    Proposal and scope

    Weeks 5–6

    A written scope that says what is included, what is not, and where contingencies are likely. Priced against the drawings, not a guess.

  5. 05

    Permitting

    Weeks 6–12

    Permits pulled directly, and every product checked for its Notice of Acceptance or Florida Product Approval.

  6. 06

    Construction

    Varies

    One point of contact, inspections at each stage, and a site that gets cleaned at the end of the day.

  7. 07

    Quality review

    Final 1–2 weeks

    We walk the work against the scope before we call it finished.

  8. 08

    Completion and handover

    Closeout

    Final inspection, a walkthrough together, and registration of the manufacturer and workmanship warranties.

Timelines vary by scope and jurisdiction.

Four financing partners, not one.

Two are consumer credit and two are property-assessed, so more than one kind of answer is possible.

Synchrony

Project Card, revolving credit

6–132

months of special financing, as Synchrony publishes it

1

card, reusable across projects

Useful if a kitchen now is likely to be followed by a bathroom or a flooring run later.

Service Finance

Fixed installment loan

30

days after completion until the first payment

0

pre-payment penalty

A natural fit for a defined, single-trade scope where the number does not move once it is set. NMLS 140908.

Ygrene

Florida PACE, not a loan

20

year maximum published residential term

Tax bill

repaid with your property taxes

Soft credit pull. Florida categories include roofing, windows and doors, HVAC, storm protection, insulation and solar.

Renew Financial

RenewPACE assessment

$250K

application fee

Live across Miami‑Dade, Broward and Palm Beach. NMLS 1788120.

Elbaz Construction is not a lender and does not approve, decline or fund applications. Every rate, term and approval decision comes from the financing partner. PACE covers specific improvements; a kitchen remodel is generally not one of them.

Consumer credit

Synchrony
Project Card, revolving. 6–132 months of special financing as published. One card, reusable across projects.
Service Finance
Fixed installment loan. First payment 30 days after completion. No pre-payment penalty.

The usual route for kitchens and bathrooms.

Property-assessed (PACE)

Ygrene
Not a loan: repaid with property taxes. Up to a 20-year published residential term. Soft credit pull.
Renew Financial
RenewPACE. Up to $250K published, and up to 20% of property value. No application fee.

For qualifying improvements such as roofing, impact windows and storm protection.
